points.text: MoE-specific defenses not explored; dormant-expert pruning discussion shallow.
Persistence under domain adaptation, instruction tuning, RL fine-tuning or updates untested.
Limited evidence that releasing poisoned MoE checkpoints is feasible in real supply chains.
No demonstration in a complete deployment pipeline such as hosted API.
Dominating-expert definition ignores other experts.
Theorem 4.1 is a trivial observation that large outputs dominate.
Unclear how much of the model is trained in the infection step.
Objective (9) is symmetric; nothing enforces claimed roles of theta_0 and theta_a.
Utility evaluation sparse; standard LLM benchmarks needed.
Clean accuracy on tasks where dormant experts are active not evaluated.
Gaussian activation assumption unrealistic given known outliers.
Attack does not leverage Theorem 4.1; loss is standard backdoor loss.
Results only incrementally better than baselines except domain shift.
Motivation weak; framed only as not done before.
Simple per-expert testing defenses would likely fix the attack.
Untested on fine-grained MoEs with many experts (DeepSeek-style).
Text attributes effect to mechanism more strongly than ablations isolate.
Ablation differences tiny for single runs; no variance.
Clean reference is un-fine-tuned base model, inflating utility claims.
Training recipe stated inconsistently between sections.
Eq. 12 sign convention contradicts text.
Paper formatted as ACM template draft.
Same quantities differ across tables.
Weak Mixtral ASR cells undiscussed.
Section ordering slip and 'bone' typo.
Survival under quantization, pruning and MoE serving practices untested.
Stability of dormancy across user data and tasks untested.
Stronger detection defenses (trigger inversion, activation clustering, router stats) not evaluated.
Dual-use and responsible release discussion thin.
Mechanism attribution confounded with trigger optimization and parameter count.
ASR appears to include target-class inputs.
Baselines at floor on some tasks inflate margins.
Prompt-robustness claim contradicted by AGNews drop.
'Rigorously prove' overstated; strong assumptions, not linked to dormant experts.
Defense-ineffectiveness claim based on few defenses, one model.
Layer and hyperparameters selected via sweeps on evaluation data.
Stealth and transfer evaluated only on SST-2/OLMoE.
Clean-model comparison uses un-fine-tuned models.
Untested post-hoc explanations for Samsum failures and ROUGE gains.
Dormant-index sign convention contradictory.
Small numeric and naming mismatches across tables.
Wrong or weak citations.
'Less than 2%' infected fraction misleading within layer.
Theory near-tautological: quantifier mismatch, unbounded weights, linear experts; 'rigorously prove' overstated.
Gaussian assumption weakly supported by notebook citation and tiny figure.
Claim that dormant experts become dominating argued only verbally.
'First MoE backdoor' claim lacks stated search window.
Baselines limited to classical NLP backdoors; LLM-era attacks not compared.
Trigger-optimization prior work uncited; delta modest.
Several citations do not support their sentences.
Explanations of baseline failure and ROUGE gain untested.
Prompt-robustness claim overstated given AGNews drop.
Stealth 'better balance' claim contradicted by Table 6.
Baseline comparison confounded by extra trainable parameters and optimized trigger.
Baselines appear under-trained, at floor on Samsum and IMDB.
ASR definition unclear, likely includes target-class inputs.
No seeds, variance or confidence intervals.
Layer and hyperparameters tuned on test data.
Defense evaluation narrow and non-adaptive; ineffective claim overstated.
No causal ablation showing infected experts cause behavior.
'Less than 2%' fraction misleading.
Eq. 16 omits lambda; 'Tirgger' typo.
Dormant-index convention in text contradicts Eq. 12.
Numeric inconsistencies across Tables 2, 3, 4, 6, 10.

P.summary: MoE-specific defenses unexplored; simple per-expert defenses may defeat attack.
Threat-model feasibility in supply chains weak.
Training objective does not enforce claimed roles.
Clean accuracy where dormant experts are active.
Theory not used by attack design.

Q.summary: Mechanism attribution confounded by trigger optimization and trainable parameters.
Clean reference is un-fine-tuned base model.
Defense evaluation narrow; ineffectiveness claim overstated.
Theory not connected to dormant experts.
Stealth and transfer on single setting.
No causal ablation of infected experts.
